topics.topic: Whether invoice_subfolder must remain contained within the root after resolving links
questions: Must invoice_subfolder, like photo_subfolder, also resolve inside the root when it is used, or is only its written path required to be inside the root?

Does an invoice_subfolder that is lexically inside root but resolves through a link outside root remain a valid confirmed connection, or must its resolved target also stay inside root as is expressly required for photo_subfolder when used?

If invoice_subfolder is written inside the root but links to a location outside it, must the connection or a later invoice-folder read refuse it, or is resolved containment required only for photo_subfolder?

quotes:
8. The form of a subfolder: the photo and invoice subfolders are non-empty relative paths without
   `..` and are not the root itself. Separately, on each scan and placement the photo folder of the
   requested project must be a folder whose resolved path is strictly below the resolved root,
   otherwise the operation is refused with `folder_unavailable`. This second check does not run at
   the start of the service or for other projects. The deliverer never opens the invoice folder, so
   the resolved path of that folder is checked by the Cabinet Inbox when it moves to this record
   (R0-09).
judgement.why: State 2 decides that the invoice folder's resolved path is checked by the Cabinet Inbox when that product moves to ObjectConnection.

topics.topic: Which action rejects a photo subfolder that resolves outside the root
questions: Which product action refuses a photo subfolder that is written inside the root but resolves through a link outside it: the connection write, or the later action that reads the folder?
Which product action refuses the linked-outside photo folder: connection creation, “See what can be delivered”, “Place chosen photos”, or every action that reads the folder?

quotes:
8. The form of a subfolder: the photo and invoice subfolders are non-empty relative paths without
   `..` and are not the root itself. Separately, on each scan and placement the photo folder of the
   requested project must be a folder whose resolved path is strictly below the resolved root,
   otherwise the operation is refused with `folder_unavailable`. This second check does not run at
   the start of the service or for other projects. The deliverer never opens the invoice folder, so
   the resolved path of that folder is checked by the Cabinet Inbox when it moves to this record
   (R0-09).
judgement.why: State 2 assigns the resolved-containment check to each scan and placement, not to connection creation or publication marking.

topics.topic: Effect of a refused connection write on the existing connection and confirmation
questions: When an attempted connection write is refused for a subfolder written outside the root, what happens to an existing ObjectConnection and its confirmation?

quotes: | Connect an object to its folders (owner, through the agent) | a connection record the owner has confirmed; delivery becomes possible for that project | a connection whose subfolder is written to leave its root is refused, a photo folder linked outside the root is refused when it is used, and an unconfirmed connection delivers nothing | unit tests |

The agent writes the connection for a project the Registry already
issued, and sets the confirmation only for the folders the owner confirmed. When the agent later
changes the root or a subfolder it clears the confirmation in the same write, and sets it again
after the owner confirms the new folders (R0-11).

One record per object, keyed by the Registry project id and confirmed by the owner, holds the
object's photo and invoice folders. The deliverer uses it now. The Cabinet Inbox moves to it
later as a separate step.

The first version has no screen for connections. The agent writes the record after the owner
confirms the object and its folders. A change of the root or of a subfolder clears the confirmation,
and delivery stops until the owner confirms again.
judgement.divergence: One implementation validates before mutation and leaves the existing confirmed ObjectConnection unchanged; another clears its confirmation or stores part of the attempted change before refusing, which the owner and subsequent delivery callers notice.
judgement.why: The texts require refusal of the invalid write but do not say whether that failed action is atomic with respect to an existing connection.

witness.initial: A Registry project has one confirmed ObjectConnection whose current root and subfolders are valid.
events: The owner proposes a changed subfolder whose written path leaves the root.
The agent performs Connect an object to its folders with that proposed change.
The calling flow subsequently asks what can be delivered for the project.
outcomes: The invalid change is refused before mutation, so the old confirmed connection remains and delivery can use it.
The invalid change is refused after the existing connection is cleared or altered, so the project is unconfirmed or its connection is unusable and delivery stops.

topics.topic: Whether owner confirmation covers stored paths only or their resolved directories
questions: Does the owner's confirmation attach only to the stored path values, or also to the filesystem directories to which those paths and links resolve?

quotes:
6. A change of an object's root or subfolder writes `assignment_confirmed` false (R0-11). An
   operation on a project with no connection is refused with `unknown_project`, and one with an
   unconfirmed connection with `connection_not_confirmed`. This is decided by the service, not by
   the caller.

8. The form of a subfolder: the photo and invoice subfolders are non-empty relative paths without
   `..` and are not the root itself. Separately, on each scan and placement the photo folder of the
   requested project must be a folder whose resolved path is strictly below the resolved root,
   otherwise the operation is refused with `folder_unavailable`. This second check does not run at
   the start of the service or for other projects. The deliverer never opens the invoice folder, so
   the resolved path of that folder is checked by the Cabinet Inbox when it moves to this record
   (R0-09).
judgement.why: State 2 makes stored root or subfolder changes clear confirmation, while a later unsafe resolved photo-folder target causes scan and placement refusal rather than changing the confirmation.
